# Introduction to the Bootcamp

## Welcome Scholars!
* **Who are we?** 28 MSc and PhD candidates across SUA, UDSM, NM-AIST, and SUZA.
* **The Goal**: Build reproducible data pipelines for your master's and doctoral theses.
* **Our Motto**: *"Bring Your Own Data (BYOD)"* — by Friday, your own datasets will be inside R pipelines.

## Why R instead of Excel?
* **Reproducibility**: If you update your data, your analysis and figures update in 1-click.
* **Efficiency**: Spend less time on manual copy-pasting and formatting.
* **Scope**: Advanced statistics, spatial GIS, and automated reports all live in the same ecosystem.

---

# Setting Up the Workspace

## Project-Centric Workflow
* Avoid using `setwd("C:/Users/name/Desktop/folder")` — this breaks when sharing code!
* Use **RStudio Projects** (`.Rproj`) to define your working directory.
* Use the `here` package for robust relative paths:
  ```r
  library(here)
  data <- read.csv(here("data", "my_dataset.csv"))
  ```

## Recommended Folder Structure
```
my_thesis_project/
├── data/           # Raw and cleaned data (read-only)
├── scripts/        # R scripts or Quarto files
├── outputs/        # Saved figures, tables, and reports
└── my_project.Rproj
```

# Introduction to Tidy Data

## What is Tidy Data?
Hadley Wickham's definition:

> "Tidy datasets are all alike, but every messy dataset is messy in its own way."

1. **Variables** in columns.
2. **Observations** in rows.
3. **Values** in individual cells.

## Visualizing Untidy vs. Tidy Data

### Untidy (Wide)
| Site | Year_2024 | Year_2025 |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Site A | 15.2 | 18.1 |
| Site B | 10.4 | 12.3 |

### Tidy (Long)
| Site | Year | Value |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Site A | 2024 | 15.2 |
| Site A | 2025 | 18.1 |
| Site B | 2024 | 10.4 |
| Site B | 2025 | 12.3 |

# Importing Tabular Data

## Essential Packages
Load the core tidyverse packages:
```r
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

## Reading Files
* **CSV Files**:
  ```r
  my_data <- read_csv(here("data", "survey_results.csv"))
  ```
* **Excel Sheets**:
  ```r
  my_data <- read_excel(here("data", "field_records.xlsx"), sheet = "Site1")
  ```
